wins.text: Q3 adjusted operating income grew 12% YoY, with Federal Express segment up 17% despite USPS contract expiration headwind of $180M and ~$70M severe weather impact
DRIVE savings reached $600M in Q3, up from $540M in Q2 and $390M in Q1, on track to hit $2.2B incremental FY25 target and $4B total vs FY23 baseline
Federal Express package volumes grew 5% YoY — highest year-over-year ADV growth since Q4 FY21 — with Ground volumes up 7% and international export packages up 8%
Onboarding nearly $400M in new annualized healthcare revenue over next 90 days, exiting FY25 with ~$9B in healthcare revenue; 75% tied to bundled FedEx Surround customers
Returned $2.5B in share repurchases YTD, on track for $3.8B total shareholder returns in FY25 including dividends; CapEx reduced to $4.9B from $5.2B last year

risks.text: FY25 adjusted EPS guidance cut to $18.00–$18.60 from prior $19.00–$20.00 range, citing B2B weakness, inflationary cost pressures, and global trade policy uncertainty

FedEx Freight operating profit declined $80M YoY in Q3; LTL average daily shipments down 5% and weight per shipment down 3% due to soft U.S. industrial economy, with headwinds expected to continue in Q4

Revenue net-of-costs headwind now projected at $1.1B for FY25, $400M worse than prior forecast, driven by international export yield pressure and greater-than-expected demand shift to lower-yielding deferred services
Inflationary pressures on cost base — including PT costs during peak and employee wages — higher than previously planned and described as persistent going forward

Uncertainty around global trade policy, tariffs, and potential de minimis rule changes creating demand visibility challenges, with management noting no significant pull-forward but acknowledging APAC volatility in late February/early March

guidance_items.detail: FY25 adjusted EPS lowered to $18.00–$18.60 from prior $19.00–$20.00 range; midpoint implies ~3% adjusted EPS growth YoY
FY25 revenue now expected flat to down slightly vs. prior year; Q4 Federal Express revenue expected essentially flat YoY, Freight revenue expected down YoY but moderating sequentially
Revenue net-of-costs headwind revised to $1.1B, $400M worse than prior forecast; $400M headwind from international export yield pressure and deferred mix shift
FY25 CapEx now $4.9B, down $300M from FY24's $5.2B; FY26 aircraft CapEx commitment of ~$1B reaffirmed
DRIVE savings target of $2.2B incremental for FY25 reaffirmed; annualized run rate to exceed $2.2B exiting Q4

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: De minimis shipment exposure and revenue impact from potential rule changes — not proactively addressed in prepared remarks
Specific quantification of inflationary cost pressures and their stickiness going forward — mentioned only broadly in prepared remarks
FedEx Freight CEO search and external vs. internal leadership succession — not mentioned in prepared remarks
